newsitem.title: UK: Ecu bonds face rough ride until EMU doubts unravel.
newsitem.headline: Ecu bonds face rough ride until EMU doubts unravel.

text.p: Ecu bonds face a turbulent ride in the coming weeks as the storm over a European single currency continues to blow. But long-term rewards are still on the cards, analysts said.

The Lefts swing into power in France this week, and the spat over Germany's plan to revalue reserves, dealt a blow to European debt markets on Monday. Ecu bonds were hit harder as they trailed France and Germany.

By Tuesday bonds were back up again. But with many in the market worried about the possibility of a soft euro or a delay to the whole project, further Ecu bond losses can be expected in the near term, economists said.
Investors should stick to shorts, look for safe trades, or keep out of Ecu altogether for a while, they said.
Weve been recommending investors to be underweight in Ecu and OATs. The risk/reward is not worth it at the moment," said David Brickman, European economist at Yamaichi International Europe here.
A trader at a U.S. investment bank in London was more blunt. The downside risks are colossal compared to what the upside gains are.

By 1116 GMT, June Ecu bond futures on the MATIF were at 94.88, up 42 basis points on the day, and up from a 93.50 low on Monday. The 5.50 percent Ecu bond due 2007 was at 94.90, to yield 6.2 percent, versus 94.45 Monday.

Ecu bonds, traded mainly from France, tend to mirror OATs and to a certain extent Bunds. The 10-year Ecu/Bund yield spread narrowed to around 25 basis points in May from 50 in April. The spread was at 33 bp on Tuesday.
Traders said convergence would likely resume once doubts over EMU (European economic and monetary union) unravelled and the stance of France and Germany became clear.
But in the meantime a phase of widening could be expected.

Some analysts say that even a softer and broader euro should put a positive spin on Ecu bonds. The Ecu market also tends to benefit with high yielders such as Italy when the outlook favours a broad intake to EMU in 1999 - a scenario favoured by the French socialist leader Lionel Jospin who swept to victory in Sundays election.
Germanys gold reserves plan to plug a budget hole would pave the way for a widespread fudging of the EMU criteria and give scrope for further bond convergence, analysts said.
Yamaichis Brickman said over the long term the Ecu/Bund spread should shrink to 15 basis points and the Ecu/OAT to 30 from around 40 now.
But higher interest rates if the euro were to be softer could shift convergence towards peripheral yields. And near term, analysts said Ecu spreads could surrender some of their recent gains.
I dont think we're up against a major blow-out, said Mary Bloem, Ecu bond strategist at Paribas Capital Markets in London. But I think spreads will widen.
She forecast the Ecu/OAT spread to spiral back up to a peak earlier this year of around 55 basis points.
People will want to see exactly what the attitude of the new French government will be towards EMU and also how things develop in Germany.

Germanys reaction to a new French governments budget plans would be crucial for investor sentiment. Jospins campaign promise to cut unemployment is likely to clash with President Jacques Chirac's EMU ambitions.
If the Germans turn around and say 'No, a flexible interpretation is not on the cards', then we have a problem, said Yamaichis Brickman.
A delay in EMU would jolt the Ecu spreads higher, but even under that scenario convergence should soon resume as the market digests a new start date, he said.
The downside should also be protected by a strong domestic presence in French bonds which keeps the market somewhat immune to EMU shocks, analysts said.
